These results have shown the algorithm is robust and our fabricated samples for the dataset are quite uniform and representative. Figure 7.6. Voc, Jsc, FF prediction results based on enlarged dataset consists of degraded cells and raw fresh cells. We have also investigated the influence of degraded cells on the algorithm. Various samples are manually degraded by overheating them under 80,100,120,150oC under 30 minutes and 60 minutes. Degraded samples are measured for % Transmission, PL, and TrPL under the same laser system. A new dataset with more than 300 samples is generated. Under the same predicting algorithm under 0.0001 gradient learning step and after 20000 epochs, prediction results are shown in Fig. 7.6. For those original undegraded samples, more consistent prediction results are shown. For those degraded data predictions, the prediction results clearly show a difference between those degraded cells versus those pristine cells, with a prediction error fluctuation from 5% to 50%. As it is not necessary to achieve how badly the cell is performed, the results show clear evidence of how the algorithm is robust in predicting various cell performances together as a classifier algorithm in sorting pristine and degraded cells. The as-developed algorithm is further proved to be robust when overpredicting the number of unknown samples even with 10 times less number in the training dataset. To overcome the shortage of the black-box model which cannot obtain a possible connection between the input Page 43 of 54 DE-EE0009512 Massachusetts Institute of Technology physical parameters with the numerical prediction results, we have also introduced the linear/polynomial regression (LR/PR) algorithms to interpret the weights of each parameter. Instead of inputting the three spectrums into the algorithm, we selectively chose the 20 representative parameters, described below. For %Transmission, we choose the maximum %T between the wavelength of 650nm to 950nm; the wavelength corresponds to the maximum %T; the wavelength of 20% of the largest %T, the wavelength of 80% of the largest %T, and the average wavelength between 20%T to 80%T. For PL, we choose the peak starting wavelength; peak starting intensity; peak maximum wavelength; peak maximum intensity; peak ending wavelength; peak ending intensity; 20% wavelength on the increasing curve; 80% wavelength on the increasing curve; 20% wavelength on the decreasing curve and 80% wavelength on the decreasing curve. For the TrPL, we choose the maximum TrPL intensity on the original data plot; we do two linear fits for the semi-log plot with each of the fitting equations y = ax+b.
